title: Canonical completed compact-support Frobenius comparison and representative compositor
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. For finite-type $k_0$-schemes $X_0,Y_0$ and a morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ with a compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ [def-nagata-compactification], use the middle model, its maps over $k_0$, and geometric-fibre conventions of [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology]. Base change both factors to obtain the geometric compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$, retaining the middle model. Geometric Frobenius commutes with these geometric-fibre maps, with the normalization of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. Use the actual completed coefficient sheaves, exact ring-module inverse images $P_h$, derived proper direct images and exact open extensions of [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison]. Put $\Phi_T=P_{F_T}$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $F_T$. Write all functor composites below using $\mathbin{\diamond}$ in execution order (first the left functor, then the right functor). Its coefficient-normalized pullback square is
$$\delta_h:P_h\mathbin{\diamond}\Phi_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_V\mathbin{\diamond}P_h,$$
formed by the inverse-image composition constraints and naturality of geometric Frobenius along $h$. Let $m_j:\Phi_U\mathbin{\diamond}j_!\to j_!\mathbin{\diamond}\Phi_V$ be its open-adjunction mate, and $m_p:Rp_*\mathbin{\diamond}\Phi_Y\to\Phi_V\mathbin{\diamond}Rp_*$ its proper direct-image mate. Both are invertible since the Frobenius maps are isomorphisms. Put $H_c=j_!\mathbin{\diamond}Rp_*$. Define the canonical compact-support comparison
$$\Gamma_c:H_c\mathbin{\diamond}\Phi_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_X\mathbin{\diamond}H_c$$
by first whiskering $m_p$ on the left by $j_!$, then whiskering $m_j^{-1}$ on the right by $Rp_*$, with the canonical associators. Ordinary Frobenius inverse image preserves derived completeness, finite-level constructibility and the common finite cohomology interval of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; it computes completed inverse image because it is an exact equivalence preserving the actual Roos completion map.

For two composable separated finite-type model morphisms $f_0,g_0$ and arbitrary compactifications of them and their composite, identify the fibre of the composite with the composite of the fibres by base-change functoriality. Define $A_{g,f,K}:Rg_!^\mathrm{amb}Rf_!^\mathrm{amb}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!^\mathrm{amb}K$ on every integral constructible input by conjugating the canonical integral compositor of [lem-zl-field-shriek-composition-qcqs] with the projection-normalized realizations of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The conjugation first applies $Rg_!^\mathrm{amb}$ to the realization for $f$, then the realization for $g$, then the integral compositor, then the inverse composite realization. This definition fixes the whole completed map, not just its finite evaluations.

source.place: Composition constraint, item (3) of prop-functor-package; canonical Frobenius structures from lem-fix-weil-operations

proof.text: Apply Over.pullback to the compactification factorization and use map_comp, then take underlying scheme maps. MorphismProperty.overPullbackMap transports properness and the open-immersion property. The same map_comp proves zlFiberMap_comp. These arguments include empty schemes.

For any scheme isomorphism g and coefficient system R, construct the pro-etale site equivalence from postcomposition and base change. The sheaf adjunction unit is invertible; its composite with the direct image of the coefficient isomorphism is therefore invertible. After forgetting commutativity this gives a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Apply SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence to it and its inverse, verifying the two compatibility equations componentwise by naturality, inverse equations and the triangle identity. This proves that the actual ringed module direct image is an equivalence, hence its left adjoint is an equivalence. Functor.isEquivalence_mapDerivedCategory gives equivalence of the specified ordinary derived pullback.

Apply the preceding equivalence to geometric Frobenius on the source, middle model and target. The existing isIso_inverseMate_of_equivalences theorem proves invertibility of the prescribed open mate. The existing upstream isIso_mateEquiv_of_isEquivalence theorem, the equivalence/equivalence specialization of the general mate result, proves invertibility of the prescribed proper mate. Both use the original normalized square without changing its components.

Geometric Frobenius is an isomorphism, hence a quasi-compact open immersion. Its geometric-fibre residue fields have invertible l by sfWeilPrimeInvertible. Specialize the existing frameworkOpenPullRealization to this automorphism. The constructible integral pullback lands in the defining full subcategory; transport its property across the inverse realization component using sfIntegralConstructible_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms. This proves zlAmbientFrobenius_constructible with its original hypotheses and the actual completed coefficient system.

Retain the specified compact-support comparison, using the two invertible mates in proper-then-open order, and retain the completed compositor obtained by conjugating the integral compositor through the three projection-normalized support realizations. No comparison definition is changed.

proof_origin.place: Canonical Frobenius comparison: site and module equivalences, existing forward and inverse mate theorems, and the normalized framework open-pullback realization applied to Frobenius.
